title: Judges 20
paragraphs: ¹ All the Israelites came out as one, from Dan to Beersheba and throughout the land of Gilead, and assembled before the LORD at Mizpah. ² The leaders of all the people and all the tribes of Israel took their places in the assembly of God's people — four hundred thousand soldiers armed with swords. ³ (The Benjamites heard that the Israelites had gone up to Mizpah.) Then the Israelites said, "Tell us — how did this terrible thing happen?" ⁴ The Levite, the husband of the murdered woman, answered: "I and my concubine came to Gibeah in Benjamin territory to spend the night. ⁵ During the night the men of Gibeah came after me and surrounded the house. They intended to kill me. They raped my concubine, and she died.

⁶ "I took my concubine's body, cut her in pieces, and sent her throughout all the territory of Israel, because they committed this vile and outrageous act in Israel. ⁷ You are all Israelites — speak up and decide what should be done." ⁸ All the people rose as one and declared, "None of us will go home. Not a single one of us will return to his house. ⁹ This is what we'll do to Gibeah: we'll go up against it by lot, ¹⁰ taking ten men out of every hundred from all the tribes of Israel — a hundred from a thousand, a thousand from ten thousand — to gather provisions for the army. When the force arrives at Gibeah in Benjamin, they will repay them for all the outrage they have committed in Israel."

¹¹ So all the Israelites came together united against the city. ¹² The tribes of Israel sent messengers throughout the tribe of Benjamin, saying, "What is this terrible thing that has happened among you? ¹³ Hand over those scoundrels in Gibeah so we can put them to death and purge this evil from Israel." But the Benjamites refused to listen to their fellow Israelites. ¹⁴ Instead, they gathered from their towns at Gibeah to fight the Israelites. ¹⁵ At that time the Benjamites mustered from their towns twenty-six thousand swordsmen, plus seven hundred elite fighters from Gibeah itself.

¹⁶ Among all these warriors were seven hundred specially chosen left-handed men, every one of whom could sling a stone and hit a target within a hair's width without missing. ¹⁷ The Israelites, not counting Benjamin, mustered four hundred thousand swordsmen, all experienced soldiers. ¹⁸ The Israelites went up to Bethel and consulted God. They asked, "Which tribe should attack Benjamin first?" The LORD answered, "Judah shall go first." ¹⁹ The Israelites rose the next morning and took up positions against Gibeah. ²⁰ The Israelite army marched out to fight Benjamin and drew up their battle lines at Gibeah.

²¹ The Benjamites came out of Gibeah and struck down twenty-two thousand Israelites in the field that day. ²² But the Israelite soldiers rallied and took up their positions again in the same place as the first day. ²³ (They had gone up and wept before the LORD until evening, and had asked, "Should we go and fight our brother Benjamin again?" The LORD said, "Go up against him.") ²⁴ The Israelites advanced against the Benjamites the second day. ²⁵ Again Benjamin came out from Gibeah to meet them and cut down another eighteen thousand Israelites — all of them armed soldiers.

²⁶ Then all the Israelites, the whole army, went up to Bethel and sat weeping before the LORD. They fasted that day until evening and offered burnt offerings and fellowship offerings to the LORD. ²⁷ The Israelites inquired of the LORD — for the ark of the covenant of God was there in those days, ²⁸ and Phinehas son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, was serving before it — asking, "Should we go out once more to fight our brother Benjamin, or should we stop?" The LORD answered, "Go, for tomorrow I will give them into your hands." ²⁹ Israel set an ambush around Gibeah. ³⁰ The Israelites went up against the Benjamites on the third day and took their positions against Gibeah as before.

³¹ The Benjamites came out against the army and were drawn away from the city. They began inflicting casualties as before, killing about thirty Israelites in the open fields — along the roads leading to Bethel and Gibeah. ³² The Benjamites thought, "We're defeating them as before." But the Israelites had said, "Let's retreat and draw them away from the city toward the roads." ³³ All the Israelites moved from their positions and formed up at Baal-tamar, while those in the ambush burst out from their positions west of Gibeah. ³⁴ Ten thousand elite Israelite fighters launched a direct assault on Gibeah. The fighting was fierce, and the Benjamites did not realize that disaster was closing in on them. ³⁵ The LORD struck down Benjamin before Israel, and the Israelites killed twenty-five thousand one hundred Benjamite swordsmen that day.

³⁶ The Benjamites saw that they were beaten — the Israelites had given ground only because they trusted the men in the ambush they had set near Gibeah. ³⁷ Those in ambush made a sudden dash into Gibeah and swept through the city, killing everyone with the sword. ³⁸ The prearranged signal between the main Israelite force and those in ambush was a great cloud of smoke rising from the city. ³⁹ When the Israelites turned back in the fighting, the Benjamites had already killed about thirty of them, thinking, "We're winning — just like the first battle!" ⁴⁰ But then the signal column of smoke began rising from the city. The Benjamites looked back, and the whole city was going up in flames.

⁴¹ When the Israelites turned back to attack, the Benjamites panicked, for they could see that disaster had overtaken them. ⁴² They retreated before the Israelites toward the desert road, but they could not escape the battle. The Israelites who came out of the towns cut them down right there. ⁴³ They had the Benjamites surrounded; they chased them down and easily trampled them in the area east of Gibeah. ⁴⁴ Eighteen thousand Benjamites fell — all of them fighting men. ⁴⁵ The rest turned and fled toward the desert to the rock of Rimmon. The Israelites cut down five thousand more along the roads, then pursued them as far as Gidom and killed another two thousand.

⁴⁶ In all, twenty-five thousand Benjamite swordsmen fell that day — all of them warriors. ⁴⁷ But six hundred men escaped to the desert and took refuge at the rock of Rimmon, where they stayed for four months. ⁴⁸ Then the Israelite army turned back against the remaining Benjamites and put to the sword every person in the towns, including the animals and everything else they found. They also set fire to every town they came to.
